text: Your “Lead Specialist” nameplate has arrived. It proudly reads “Lead Specalist.” A new one takes a month, at your expense.
origin: You took the promotion for the nameplate

text: The department found out you report to the boss on who left for lunch when. Nobody invites you to lunch anymore, and the chat now says “Shh, the walls have ears.”
origin: You became the boss’s “eyes and ears”

text: The organizers sent the program: you’re the last speaker, at 7:40 p.m., right after the banquet. Slides are due by morning, and so far you only have a title.
origin: You agreed to speak at the conference

text: The boss arrived at the end of the stand-up you ran and learned the department unanimously voted for a four-day week. The minutes have already gone out.
origin: Morning: you ran stand-up for the boss

text: The deputy presented your briefing and thanked you in front of everyone: “Our colleague prepared this.” Your own manager is watching you very closely.
origin: You prepared a briefing for the deputy

text: The boss remembers who showed him that invite. Now you schedule all the stand-ups, and their timing is your fault too. The first one is tomorrow at 8:30.
origin: You showed the boss his own invite

text: An invoice arrived for a year of coffee, three packs a day. It was in the fine print on the back of the paper you signed for the trial batch.
origin: You signed for the free coffee trial

text: The client you moved the deadline a week earlier for writes: “We’ve been thinking — let’s go back to the original date. And add a couple of edits.”
origin: You moved the client’s deadline earlier

text: 11:40 p.m. The client calls to ask what font was on slide four. Apparently he read the “contractor is always available” clause more carefully than you did.
origin: You signed the “always available” clause

text: Security wants to know why your chair has a blanket with a tender bidder’s logo on it. The blanket is warm; the question is very cold.
origin: You took a blanket from a bidder

text: The client’s bosses loved “his” presentation and expect the same at the annual meeting. The client writes to you again: “Help, my voice still hasn’t come back.”
origin: You voiced the client who lost his voice

text: The fifty pallets of paper you signed for are blocking the emergency exit. The fire inspector arrives in an hour; the paper isn’t going anywhere.
origin: You signed for 50 pallets of paper

text: Your personalized T-shirt is ready. On the back, in big letters: “Team Captain.” By tradition, the captain runs ten kilometers, not five.
origin: You signed up for the company run

text: HR at your former colleague’s new job calls: “You praised him so highly, and in a week he made one presentation. With no slides.” They want an explanation.
origin: You praised a slacker in a reference

text: The talent show is today. The host announces your act as “the elevator hit,” and the sound engineer asks what key the elevator usually sings in.
origin: You agreed to perform at the talent show

text: The newbie you gave a tour now treats you as the help desk. 23 questions so far today, the latest: “Are you new here too?”
origin: You gave the newbie a tour

text: First “Leadership School” homework: “Inspire your department by Monday.” The department can already sense it’s about to be inspired.
origin: You joined the “Leadership School”

text: Last day of the 360 review. The system reminds you: 920 fields left empty. Colleagues are already asking why they got “zero for teamwork.”
right: Fill it in honestly all night
origin: You put off the 360 review

text: Thursday. Gennady, the cactus you adopted, is due for watering today. The office manager is already making rounds with a list and a watering can.
left: Say Gennady is on a diet
origin: You adopted Gennady the cactus

text: Your neighbor’s heater under your desk is on full blast. Your feet are in the tropics, your head is at the office, and the power strip is clicking suspiciously.
origin: You let a heater under your desk

text: The yogurt investigation has hit forty messages in the chat. Prime suspect: the head of the department, who has already written “Let’s get back to work.”
origin: You posted the yogurt evidence in chat

text: Your neighbor is looking for his favorite pen and made a list of suspects. You’re at the top — after all, the pen is in your hand right now.
origin: You borrowed a neighbor’s pen forever

text: Morning. Security won’t let you in without a badge, and the chat says stand-up has already started. The guard suggests you wait until someone identifies you.
origin: Evening: you left your badge on the desk

text: After your heroic trash run, the office manager hung a schedule in the kitchen. Next to every day of the week — your name.
origin: You took out the trash for everyone

text: The minutes you took became the project’s key document. The host demands you add that he proposed all of it back in March.
origin: You agreed to take the meeting minutes

text: One of the three tasks you got from someone else’s meeting minutes turned out to be a six-month project. The deadline in the minutes: Friday.
origin: You accepted tasks from the minutes

text: The follow-up meeting you organized ended with the conclusion “Let’s meet again.” Everyone is looking at you again.
origin: You agreed to organize a follow-up

text: Your message about how badly everything is organized got forwarded to management. The reply came fast: “Great analysis. So you’ll organize it.”
origin: You sent an angry message to the chat

text: The department demands the lasagna recipe from yesterday’s email. Nobody ever asked for the report, and the calendar already says “Tasting, Friday.”
origin: You joked your way out with a lasagna photo

text: 8:00. The meeting you got up at six for has been rescheduled for the fifth time. The assistant writes cheerfully: “How about tomorrow at 7:30?”
origin: You agreed to an 8:00 a.m. meeting

text: The goat mascot ate three badges and a corner of a contract. Accounting asks which budget line the hay should go under.
left: Send the goat to a farm
origin: You kept the baby goat as a mascot

text: The parrot by your desk learned a second phrase: “I’ll do it tomorrow.” It says it in your voice, and only when your manager is around.
origin: You let the parrot live by your desk

text: The CEO pulled your “double salary” note off the wishing tree and announced: granted. Salary doubled, duties quadrupled.
origin: You wished for “double salary”

text: The founder’s bust now stands in the lobby. It looks so much like you that visitors greet it as you. Your manager asks you to “give tours.”
origin: You posed for the founder’s bust

text: Room 404 has been found: it holds an archive of reports nobody has opened since 2009. Only you have the key, and accounting already knows.
right: Make it a secret meeting room
origin: You went looking for Room 404

text: The cat you took home slept on your head all night and in the morning rode back to the office in your bag. The team is thrilled; the office manager isn’t.
right: Let the cat stay at the office
origin: You took the office cat home

text: Your sister is thrilled: “Since it’s on your way, could you pick him up too? At 5:30.” The daycare is still on the other side of town.
origin: Morning: you took Tyoma to daycare

text: Beach tickets bought. One small thing: the flight is on the day the quarterly report is due, and your manager doesn’t know yet.
origin: You bought beach vacation tickets

text: 9:00, stand-up. After last night’s board games, you call the project “our Mars colony” and demand someone roll the dice. Everyone looks intrigued.
origin: You played board games until midnight

text: The tulle snowflake was a hit. Your sister writes: “The daycare loved it! Can you make seven more? For the whole group, by Friday.”
origin: You sewed a tulle snowflake costume

text: 6:00. The new-life alarm is ringing. The old life is begging for five more minutes. Get up?
right: Get up and do it all
origin: You set the alarm for 6:00 a.m.

text: The massage therapist found a “year-end report knot” in your back and booked you a ten-session course. Each at 6:30 p.m., right when your manager loves to schedule calls.
origin: You slipped off to a 6:30 p.m. massage

text: The policy you signed without reading contains a clause: “The undersigned shall train the department.” The training is tomorrow.
origin: You signed the policy without reading it

text: The client happily accepted the quote with prices from two years ago and has already paid. Finance asks who gave them a thirty percent discount.
left: Ask the client to pay extra
origin: You sent a quote with old prices

text: The director replied to your report: “Great revenue! I’ll announce it at the shareholders’ meeting.” The error — off by a factor of ten — is still there.
origin: You stayed quiet about a report error

text: The contractor whose work you signed off as 100% done has stopped answering. The remaining 40% of the work is now on you.
origin: You signed off on 100% of the work

text: The task was estimated at 3 points after all, and it’s now on day three. The team lead quietly comes over and asks: “How did you know about the forty?”
origin: You held out for 40 points, not 3

text: The neighboring team loves the $40 phase and wants two more “within the same budget.” The budget is already bursting at the seams.
origin: You squeezed another team’s phase into budget

text: Your manager is looking for Igor, who’s been “in the meeting room for a while.” The meeting room is hosting the CEO’s meeting, and Igor isn’t there. The manager heads your way again.
origin: You covered for Igor being late

text: Oksana’s debt log already lists three staplers. Today she came for the hole punch and wants to know what that notebook on your desk is.
origin: You started a log of Oksana’s debts

text: The presentation Ira bought you coffee for is 60 slides, and it turns out you’re presenting it too. Ira is bringing a second cup.
origin: You took Ira’s coffee and her presentation

text: Philip’s “interesting” project: a warehouse out of town, the key is with the watchman, the watchman is on vacation. Meanwhile, Philip finished your reconciliation in an hour.
origin: You swapped tasks with Philip

text: An hour later the whole department knows your salary, and Galya has already asked the manager for “what some people get.” The manager wants to see you.
origin: You told Tonya your salary

text: Lida’s seedlings have exploded: the tomatoes reach the blinds, and a suspicious cactus has bloomed and smells. Lida is back tomorrow.
left: Hand some out to the team
right: Care for them like your own
origin: You took care of Lida’s seedlings

text: Since you have the admin password, there’s a line at your desk: the printer, two passwords, and an accountant whose “internet disappeared along with the monitor.”
origin: You took the admin password

text: The sysadmin promised nothing would break. Your bookmarks, passwords and email signature broke — it now reads “Sent from my calculator.”
origin: You let IT install the new system

text: Your manager noticed your 11:47 p.m. email and praised you in front of everyone: “That’s the example to follow!” Now he expects you to be online at night.
origin: You scheduled an email for 11:47 p.m.

text: Your manager glanced over your shoulder at your script that does a week’s work in five minutes. He says: “Excellent, then you’ll take on three more departments.”
origin: You secretly wrote a helper script

text: The department’s first training. You ask the AI a simple question in front of everyone, and it apologizes at length, then writes a poem about the report.
origin: You volunteered to teach everyone AI

text: After your warning, the team is scared of every email. The real email from accounting about bonuses was unanimously deleted as phishing.
origin: You warned the team about phishing
